text:
📈 Gate’s TradFi Volume Surges 55% WoW as Semis and Metals Take Over

@Gate TradFi trading volume jumped to $18.1B between August 3 - 10, up 55% from the previous week. The growth also came with a noticeable change in what traders were buying.

Semiconductors dominated equity activity. SanDisk generated about $5.6B in volume, followed by SK Hynix at $4.23B and SpaceX at $3.51B. Those three names made up most of the equity volume in that period, while CRCL and GOOGL were much smaller at roughly $146 million and $91 million.

The Korean-stock numbers are especially concentrated. SK Hynix accounted for about $4.2B in volume over the period, compared with just $62 million for Samsung Electronics. So while Korean equities are gaining traction on Gate, almost all of that increase came from SK Hynix, amid strong demand for AI and memory-chip exposure.

Trading is also spreading beyond equities. Metals rose to 27% of total volume, up from roughly 9% at the beginning of August. XAU and XAG were among the main contributors, alongside CL. 

The picture is fairly clear: Gate’s TradFi volume is growing, and the asset mix is getting broader. Equities are still heavily concentrated, though. AI-linked stocks, memory-chip names and other high-beta trades continue to draw most of the activity.

text:
👀 Bitcoin rallies, then retail deposits spike on @Gate

Bitcoin climbed from ~$64,000 to $80,000, and retail inflows to Gate picked up soon after the price increase.  

Between August 23 and 30, there were more than 11 large spikes in retail deposit volume. On August 29, hourly deposits hit $11.33M, the highest level recorded this year.  

The first explanation is pretty straightforward: profit-taking. Bitcoin runs higher, traders send coins to an exchange, and some of that supply is likely getting ready to sell. But exchange inflows aren't as simple as they used to be. 

@Gate  now gives traders access to crypto, stocks and commodities. So those deposits don't necessarily translate directly into BTC sell pressure. Some traders may be cashing out, while others could simply be moving capital around or getting ready to trade somewhere else.
